name: LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS MnemOS Clarity Cognitive Support Sys
description:
The MnemOS Clarity is LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS' flagship elderly cognitive support BCI, engineered specifically for patients presenting with mild-to-moderate neurodegenerative conditions including Alzheimer's-spectrum dementia, vascular cognitive impairment, and age-associated memory consolidation failure. The device deploys a 512-electrode high-resolution hippocampal interface combined with a prefrontal scaffold array, working in concert to provide real-time memory encoding assistance — intercepting failing consolidation events and routing them through an onboard neuromorphic co-processor that reconstructs and re-presents memory traces during retrieval attempts. The system does not store raw memory data on-device; instead, it maintains a dynamic pattern-completion model trained on the individual patient's neural signature over a 30-day calibration period. Integrated pharmaceutical microdosing ports allow the device to interface with LAZARUS's NeuroChem drip series, delivering targeted acetylcholine precursors and BDNF analogues at the site of hippocampal interface contact, significantly outperforming systemic pharmaceutical approaches in clinical trials.

In GLMZ, where the population skews heavily toward augmentation-extended lifespans creating an unprecedented cohort of individuals living into their 120s and 130s, dementia has become a quiet epidemic that the city's gleaming transhumanist aesthetic struggles to accommodate. The MnemOS Clarity is both a medical triumph and a cultural flashpoint — families speak of loved ones 'coming back' after installation, of grandparents who had lost decades of identity suddenly able to recognize grandchildren again. But the device also raises uncomfortable questions about authenticity and continuity of self: when a patient's memories are being pattern-completed by a neuromorphic chip, are they remembering, or being told a story the machine believes they should remember? LAZARUS's own ethics board has published three conflicting position papers on the question, none conclusive.
legality: Unrestricted (Medical) — prescription required from licensed gerontological neurologist; covered under GLMZ Elder Care Augmentation Subsidy Program (income-qualified patients)
installation_requirements: Gerontological neurologist or certified neurosurgeon; 30-day pre-installation neural baseline mapping; NeuroChem drip compatibility assessment; quarterly clinical review post-installation
rejection_risk: Moderate (8.7% in patients over 90); elevated in patients with significant cortical atrophy; LAZARUS offers a pre-screening biomarker test (MnemOS-Screen) to assess candidacy
maintenance: Monthly firmware update via clinic uplink; quarterly NeuroChem port flush and refill; annual full electrode impedance check; neuromorphic model re-training every 6 months
specifications: {"hippocampal_electrodes": 512, "prefrontal_scaffold_electrodes": 128, "neuromorphic_coprocessor": "LAZARUS NM-7 (onboard, 4 TOPS)", "memory_model": "patient-specific pattern-completion, no raw data storage", "calibration_period": "30 days", "pharmaceutical_ports": 4, "compatible_drips": "LAZARUS NeuroChem Series 3–7", "battery_life": "24 months (inductive recharge)", "connectivity": "encrypted clinic uplink only (no civilian mesh)", "approved_age_range": "55+ years", "dementia_staging_support": "MCI through moderate-stage Alzheimer's-spectrum"}
side_effects: Memory confabulation events in 6.2% of users — the neuromorphic model occasionally pattern-completes with plausible but factually incorrect memories, particularly for emotionally salient events
Emotional flattening reported in 9% of long-term users, hypothesized to result from the device smoothing over affectively charged memory gaps
Device dependency: patients who undergo removal (elective or due to rejection) experience significantly accelerated cognitive decline compared to untreated controls
cultural_context: LAZARUS markets the MnemOS Clarity almost exclusively through elder care facilities and family consultation channels, deliberately avoiding the youth-oriented augmentation culture of street clinics and body-mod parlors. The device has nonetheless developed a quiet emotional resonance in GLMZ's older residential districts, where community centers hold 'reconnection gatherings' for MnemOS patients and their families — events that are simultaneously celebrations of medical technology and grieving rituals for the versions of people that existed before installation.
known_users: Elderly patients in LAZARUS-partnered memory care facilities across GLMZ's residential tiers
Retired corporate executives whose families have paid for premium tier installation to preserve institutional knowledge
Subsidized installations in outer-corridor elder care cooperatives funded by GLMZ social welfare programs
story_hooks: A retired archivist with a MnemOS Clarity begins experiencing memories that don't belong to her — fragments that appear to be from another patient whose neural signature contaminated her model during a clinic uplink. The memories contain evidence of a corporate crime someone went to great lengths to suppress.

The party is hired to locate a missing elderly man with advanced dementia whose MnemOS was forcibly removed. Without the device he cannot communicate reliably — but his behavioral patterns suggest he is trying to lead someone somewhere specific, somewhere the chip helped him remember.

LAZARUS announces a mandatory firmware update to the MnemOS line. A small group of patients and their families are refusing the update, claiming the previous version of their loved ones — personality, memory patterns, emotional character — will be 'overwritten.' They may not be wrong.
